source_meta.issue links: Relates:outward:MC-128329:Seagrass interferes with village bridge generation
source_meta._title: Naturally-generated seagrass and kelp destroys ice

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft: Java Edition 18w20c in a new single-player Default-type world. Use Creative mode with commands enabled so the report-provided teleport command can be executed safely. Keep the world in 18w20c for the entire reproduction and do not pre-generate, edit, replace, break, or place blocks in the target area.
preconditions: Install or select the historical Java Edition snapshot Minecraft 18w20c in the Minecraft Launcher.
Use a newly created world rather than a world generated or opened in another Minecraft version.
Use the report-supported seed -3663419213315141181, supplied in the early reporter comment associated with the original report.
Set the world type to Default; do not use Superflat, Buffet, Customized, or another alternate generator.
Use Creative mode and enable commands/cheats.
Before the teleport, do not manually travel to or otherwise load the area around X=1568, Z=-1184.
Do not use the fix version 24w44a for this reproduction.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, configure or select an installation whose version is exactly Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 18w20c, then launch it.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen is open and identifies the running version as 18w20c.

steps.action: From the title screen, select Singleplayer, then select Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Set Game Mode to Creative. Ensure Allow Cheats or Allow Commands is ON so an in-game teleport command can be used.
steps.success_cue: The new world is configured for Creative mode and commands are enabled.

steps.action: Open More World Options, enter the report-supported world seed exactly as shown, and leave World Type set to Default.
steps.success_cue: The seed field contains -3663419213315141181 and the selected generator is Default.

steps.action: Select Create New World to generate and enter the world.
steps.success_cue: The player has spawned in the newly generated world in Creative mode.

steps.action: Wait at the spawn location without traveling toward the target coordinates. Continue only after nearby terrain has rendered and normal movement responds without world-loading pauses.
steps.success_cue: Spawn-area chunks are rendered, controls respond normally, and the distant target area has not been visited manually.

steps.action: Press T, using the default Open Chat control, to open the in-game chat input.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is visible and ready to accept a command.

steps.action: Enter the report-provided teleport command exactly, including the leading slash and the relative Y coordinate represented by ~, then press Enter. The command teleports the executing player to X=1568 and Z=-1184 while retaining the player's current Y coordinate; loading the distant target chunks is the world-generation trigger.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted and the player is teleported to the area around X=1568, Z=-1184.

steps.action: Do not move, place blocks, or break blocks while the destination terrain loads. Wait until the surrounding destination chunks have rendered and movement and camera controls respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The target-area terrain is fully visible, no loading screen or major chunk-loading pause remains, and the player remains near X=1568, Z=-1184.

steps.action: If the retained Y coordinate leaves the camera underwater, inside terrain, or otherwise obstructed, double-tap Space to begin Creative flight and hold Space only until the nearby ice-covered water surface can be viewed clearly; then release Space. Do not break or place any blocks and remain near the supplied X and Z coordinates.
steps.exact_input: Space, Space; then hold Space as needed
steps.success_cue: The player has an unobstructed view of the naturally generated ice-covered water terrain near X=1568, Z=-1184, with the generated blocks left untouched.

stor.handoff_condition: The newly generated destination chunks around X=1568, Z=-1184 have finished rendering in Minecraft Java Edition 18w20c, and the player has a clear view of the naturally generated ice-covered water terrain without having modified any blocks. Hand control to the observation subsystem now.
uncertainties: The report's current formal How to reproduce section is explicitly for version 1.21 and uses seed -953538683905638291 with different coordinates. Because the required recommended version is the first listed affected version, Minecraft 18w20c, this plan instead uses seed -3663419213315141181 and /tp @s 1568 ~ -1184 from the early reporter comment associated with the original 2018 report.

The comment providing seed -3663419213315141181 and coordinates X=1568, Z=-1184 does not explicitly label its Minecraft version. Its timing immediately after the original 18w20c-era report supports using it for the earliest affected version, but the version-to-seed pairing is not stated outright.

A later comment reports that X=1568, Z=-1184 led to land in version 1.13.1 and supplies X=1709, Y=64, Z=-1210 for that later version. This does not establish that the original coordinates fail in 18w20c, so the original coordinate command is preserved for the recommended version.

The report command uses ~ for Y, so the arrival altitude depends on the player's spawn altitude. Creative flight is included only as a non-destructive way to obtain a clear view if that retained altitude obstructs the target surface.

If no ice-covered water terrain is visible near the supplied coordinates after all destination chunks finish loading, stop rather than exploring randomly; that would indicate that the unlabeled seed-and-coordinate pair is not deterministic for 18w20c.

source_meta.issue links: Cloners:inward:MC-241277:Server can't generate amplified/large biomes worlds from scratch
source_meta._title: Server doesn't generate amplified / large biome worlds

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition using the unmodified vanilla dedicated server JAR for 1.16 Pre-release 1 and a matching 1.16 Pre-release 1 client. Run the server in a new, isolated directory on the same computer as the client so it can be reached through localhost. Use a Java runtime compatible with this historical version, with no mods, plugins, custom datapacks, or pre-existing world save.
preconditions: Obtain the exact vanilla dedicated server JAR for Minecraft Java Edition 1.16 Pre-release 1; do not substitute 1.16 Pre-release 6 or another later version.
Install or configure a Minecraft Java Edition client installation for the matching 1.16 Pre-release 1 version.
Install a Java runtime capable of launching the 1.16 Pre-release 1 server JAR.
Use a new test directory that does not contain a world folder or files from another server.
Review and accept the Minecraft EULA before setting eula=true.
Ensure the default Minecraft server port is available locally, or consistently use another configured port when connecting.
Do not copy a singleplayer world or an older server world into the test directory; the dedicated server must create the test world from scratch.

steps.action: Create a new, otherwise empty directory for this reproduction. Place the vanilla 1.16 Pre-release 1 dedicated server JAR in it and rename the file to server.jar for the commands below. Do not use a Bukkit, Spigot, Forge, Fabric, or otherwise modified server.
steps.success_cue: The isolated directory contains server.jar and no world save directory.

steps.action: Open a terminal or command prompt with its working directory set to the directory containing server.jar. Start the server once so that it can create its initial configuration files.
steps.success_cue: The server reports that the EULA must be accepted and then terminates without reaching the normal server-ready state.

steps.action: Confirm that eula.txt now exists. Open it in a plain-text editor, review the referenced EULA, change the EULA setting to true, save the file, and close the editor.
steps.success_cue: The saved eula.txt file contains eula=true.

steps.action: Open server.properties in a plain-text editor. If the file was not created during the initial launch, create a plain-text file with that exact filename in the server directory. Find the level-type property or add it if absent, and set its value exactly to the lowercase value supplied by the report. Remove any duplicate level-type entries, then save and close the file.
steps.success_cue: server.properties contains exactly one active level-type line, and that line reads level-type=amplified.

steps.action: While the server is stopped, read the value of level-name in server.properties. If the property is absent, treat its value as world. Confirm that no directory bearing that level name exists in the server directory. Because this is an isolated test directory, move or delete such a directory if one was accidentally generated; do not reuse it.
steps.success_cue: There is no existing save directory corresponding to the configured level-name, so the next launch must create the world from scratch.

steps.action: Perform a final configuration check before world creation: verify that eula.txt still contains eula=true and server.properties still contains level-type=amplified. Leave level-seed unchanged or blank because the report supplies no required seed. Do not make server.properties read-only.
steps.success_cue: The EULA is accepted, amplified is configured, and the configured level directory remains absent.

steps.action: From the terminal or command prompt whose working directory is the test server directory, launch the 1.16 Pre-release 1 server again. This launch is the trigger because the dedicated server is now asked to create a brand-new world while level-type is set to amplified.
steps.success_cue: The console identifies the running Minecraft server version as 1.16 Pre-release 1 or 1.16-pre1 and begins preparing or generating the configured level.

steps.action: Leave the server running and wait until initial spawn generation finishes. Do not connect or stop the server while the console is still reporting world preparation percentages.
steps.success_cue: The server console displays its normal Done message and accepts console input, indicating that initial world generation has completed.

steps.action: Start Minecraft Java Edition using a launcher installation explicitly configured for 1.16 Pre-release 1. If necessary, enable snapshot versions in the launcher's Installations area to expose pre-release versions; verify the version shown on the client title screen before continuing. ([minecraft.net](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/minecraft-1-16-pre-release-1?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft client reaches the main menu and identifies itself as 1.16 Pre-release 1 rather than a later pre-release or release.

steps.action: From the main menu select Multiplayer, choose Direct Connect, enter localhost as the server address, and select Join Server. If the server uses a non-default port, append that same port to the address as localhost:<port>. The Direct Connect path and local-address method are standard Java Edition server connection procedures. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3AMenu_screen/Java_Edition?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The client joins the dedicated server and the player appears in the newly generated Overworld.

steps.action: Do not move far from spawn yet. Wait until the terrain surrounding the player has rendered, the loading screen has disappeared, and player looking and movement controls respond normally. Keep the server and client running at this point.
steps.success_cue: The matching client is standing in fully loaded initial chunks of the fresh world generated by the dedicated server.

stor.handoff_condition: The vanilla 1.16 Pre-release 1 dedicated server has just created a brand-new world from scratch with level-type=amplified configured, the server has reached its Done state, and a matching client is connected with the initial Overworld chunks fully rendered. Begin observation of the generated world type, terrain, and relevant world-generation metadata without regenerating or replacing the world.
uncertainties: The report supplies no world seed, coordinates, game mode, operating system, memory allocation, or Java runtime build. Leave the seed blank and otherwise retain normal server defaults unless the execution environment requires a harmless infrastructure change.

The phrase “latest pre-release” in the original steps is date-relative, but the issue metadata lists only 1.16 Pre-release 1 as affected. This plan therefore uses that exact affected version and does not use the fixed 1.16 Pre-release 6.
Comments report similar behavior for largebiomes and later pre-releases, but those versions are not present in the report's Affects versions field. They are not added to affected_versions.

This plan uses the report's primary amplified variant. To execute the separately mentioned Large Biomes variant, a separate fresh server directory and fresh world would be required with level-type=largebiomes; it should not replace or reuse this amplified test world.

The exact historical server JAR download location or checksum is not supplied. The executor must independently ensure that both the server and client identify themselves as 1.16 Pre-release 1 or 1.16-pre1 before generating the world.

Depending on the server package and first-launch behavior, server.properties might not exist after the EULA-gated launch. Step 4 therefore permits creating the file before any EULA-accepted launch can generate the test world.

source_meta.issue links: Duplicate:inward:MC-239767:One block tall pointed dripstone generates excessively
source_meta._title: Clusters of dripstone (stalagmites) tend to generate abnormally frequent with thickness "tip" on tall caves

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition 1.17.1 in single-player, using a fresh Single Biome world configured as Dripstone Caves, with commands enabled and the player in Spectator mode. This plan uses the report's alternative surface reproduction route because it avoids the unguided search for a large noise cave.
preconditions: Install or make available the exact Minecraft: Java Edition version labeled "1.17.1" in the Minecraft Launcher.
Use a vanilla client with no mods or third-party datapacks that alter biome features, cave generation, terrain generation, or pointed dripstone generation.
Create a new world; do not reuse an existing world because the relevant terrain and dripstone features must be newly generated.
The report supplies no world seed or coordinates, so leave the seed unspecified and expect the exact terrain layout to vary.
Commands must be enabled so that the player can enter Spectator mode.

steps.action: Open the Minecraft Launcher, select an installation using exactly Java Edition 1.17.1, start the game, and wait for the main menu.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is open and the displayed game version is 1.17.1.

steps.action: Select "Singleplayer", then select "Create New World". Use a new world rather than opening or converting an existing save.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Select "More World Options..." and set "Allow Cheats" to "ON". Leave the seed field empty because the report does not provide a seed.
steps.success_cue: The world-options screen shows that commands are allowed and no seed has been entered.

steps.action: Use the "World Type" button repeatedly until it displays "Single Biome", then select the adjacent "Customize" button.
steps.success_cue: The biome-selection list for the Single Biome world type is open.

steps.action: Find and select the biome named "Dripstone Caves", then confirm the selection with "Done". Do not substitute another biome. If this biome is unavailable in the selected 1.17.1 installation, stop because the report does not identify the additional historical experimental setup that would be required.
steps.success_cue: The world-options screen is restored and the Single Biome customization is set to Dripstone Caves.

steps.action: Select "Create New World" to generate the fresh Dripstone Caves single-biome world.
steps.success_cue: The player has spawned in the newly generated world.

steps.action: Do not move immediately. Wait until the terrain around the spawn position has rendered, the loading overlay has disappeared, and looking or moving responds normally.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is visible without unrendered gaps and player controls respond normally.

steps.action: Press the chat key, which is T by default. Type the command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter: /gamemode spectator
steps.success_cue: The game confirms the mode change; the normal hotbar is no longer shown, flight is active, and the player can pass through solid blocks.

steps.action: Reach the top surface of the Overworld. If the player is below or inside terrain, hold the upward flight control, Space by default, until the player passes through the terrain and reaches open sky. If already above ground, rise far enough to see the surrounding topmost terrain.
steps.success_cue: Open sky and the world's exposed top surface are visible, and the player is no longer enclosed by underground blocks.

steps.action: Use the movement controls, W/A/S/D by default, to fly horizontally over previously unvisited surface terrain while keeping the ground in view. Continue until a broad area spanning multiple adjacent terrain sections has generated.
steps.success_cue: A broad stretch of newly generated surface is visible around and ahead of the player.

steps.action: Stop moving and wait until all visible surface terrain and naturally generated features have fully rendered. Do not continue while there are blank areas, temporary holes caused by loading, or delayed block updates.
steps.success_cue: The visible surface has finished rendering and movement responds normally.

steps.action: While remaining in Spectator mode, locate an exposed surface area containing multiple naturally generated pointed-dripstone patches. Fly closer or descend with the sneak/descend control, Left Shift by default, only as needed to distinguish individual pointed-dripstone blocks. Do not place, break, or modify any blocks, and do not yet classify their thickness or height.
steps.success_cue: Several naturally generated pointed-dripstone formations are visible clearly enough for their individual blocks to be inspected, while the surrounding terrain remains unmodified.

steps.action: Face an adjacent, previously unvisited portion of the same surface and fly forward into rendering range while looking toward the ground. Stop as soon as that terrain and its pointed-dripstone features have finished generating and rendering.
steps.success_cue: The newly entered surface section is fully rendered, the player is stationary in Spectator mode, and its naturally generated pointed-dripstone formations are in view.

stor.handoff_condition: A previously unvisited section of the Dripstone Caves single-biome surface has just generated and fully rendered, and the stationary Spectator-mode camera is looking at its naturally generated pointed-dripstone formations. Hand control to the observation subsystem before moving farther or modifying the terrain.
uncertainties: The report lists 1.17.1 first, so it is the required recommended version. However, the report was written during the experimental development of the 1.18 world-generation system and refers to large noise caves. The report does not identify which experimental snapshot, installation, or world-generation package was associated with its 1.17.1 entry. Preserve 1.17.1 as listed rather than silently replacing it with 21w37a.
No seed or coordinates are provided. The exact positions and density of surface pointed-dripstone patches therefore depend on random world generation.
The report does not define a quantitative minimum size for a "big/tall" cave or a precise distance for the claimed absence of nearby stalactites.

This execution plan intentionally selects the report's alternative surface route. The primary route—searching underground in Spectator mode for a large noise cave—is less deterministic without a supplied seed or coordinates.

If the selected 1.17.1 installation does not offer Dripstone Caves in the Single Biome selector or does not generate the terrain needed by the report, the missing historical experimental setup cannot be reconstructed confidently from the supplied report alone.

source_meta.issue links: Relates:inward:MC-240271:Dripstone Cave decorators are different each time ignoring world seed | Relates:inward:MC-219200:Lush Cave decorator is different each time ignoring the world seed
source_meta._title: Decorators are independent of world seed

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 21w10a in single-player. Use two separately created Single Biome worlds configured for the Lush Caves biome, both using seed -8718622960759467126. Use Creative mode with commands enabled, then Spectator mode for locating and revisiting an underground decorator-rich reference chamber. Use an unmodified vanilla client with no custom datapacks or world-generation modifications.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher is able to start the exact Java Edition snapshot 21w10a; do not use the fixed snapshot 21w43a.
Snapshots are enabled in the Minecraft Launcher installation settings if 21w10a is not already available.
No existing world is reused or copied: the reproduction requires two independently generated world saves with identical generation settings and the same seed.
Use the same client settings for both worlds. Do not add or remove datapacks, mods, or other world-generation modifiers between world creation attempts.
The executor can save the first world's reference coordinates, yaw, pitch, and screenshot for use while loading the second world.
Instructions assume the English user interface and default controls: T opens chat, F3 opens the debug overlay, F2 captures a screenshot, and Esc opens the pause menu.

steps.action: Start Minecraft Java Edition using the launcher installation for snapshot 21w10a. On the title screen, verify that the displayed version is 21w10a before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen is open and identifies the running version as 21w10a.

steps.action: Open the single-player world list and begin creating the first independent world.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is open.

steps.action: Give the first world a distinct baseline name so that it cannot be confused with the later independently generated world.
steps.success_cue: The world-name field contains MC-238073-Baseline.

steps.action: Set the first world's game mode to Creative and enable commands. Creative mode and commands are execution aids for reaching an underground reference location without changing the required seed.
steps.exact_input: Game Mode: Creative; Allow Cheats: ON
steps.success_cue: The creation screen shows Creative mode and commands/cheats enabled.

steps.action: Open the additional world-generation options and enter the report's seed exactly, including its leading minus sign.
steps.exact_input: More World Options... -> Seed for the World Generator: -8718622960759467126
steps.success_cue: The seed field contains exactly -8718622960759467126.

steps.action: Configure the world as a Single Biome world and select Lush Caves as its biome. In 21w10a, Lush Caves do not generate in the default world type, so this custom world configuration is required to expose their generated decorators in the recommended affected version.
steps.exact_input: World Type: Single Biome -> Customize -> select Lush Caves -> Done
steps.success_cue: The world-generation screen shows Single Biome configured with the Lush Caves biome.

steps.action: Leave all other world-generation settings unchanged, then create the first world.
steps.success_cue: The game leaves the creation menus and begins generating MC-238073-Baseline.

steps.action: Wait for the first world to finish loading. Do not continue while the loading screen is visible or while nearby terrain is still appearing.
steps.success_cue: The player can move normally, nearby chunks are rendered, and the pause or chat interface responds without waiting for initial world loading.

steps.action: Verify and record the world's seed using an in-game command. Press T to open chat, enter the command with its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports the seed as -8718622960759467126; save or copy this value as the seed used for the second world.

steps.action: Enter Spectator mode so the executor can pass through terrain and locate an underground Lush Caves chamber without mining or placing blocks. Press T, enter the command with its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The player is in Spectator mode, can fly, and can pass through solid blocks.

steps.action: Move to a fixed staging area away from the initially generated spawn chunks. Press T, execute the teleport command with its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The player is near X=512, Y=32, Z=512 in Spectator mode.

steps.action: Wait until the terrain around the staging area has generated and rendered. Do not start selecting the reference chamber while chunks are still visibly loading.
steps.success_cue: Underground terrain around X=512, Z=512 is visible and flight responds normally.

steps.action: While remaining in Spectator mode, fly through the nearby underground terrain until an unobstructed Lush Caves chamber is visible. Prefer a chamber containing several clearly identifiable generated decorative features, such as moss coverage, azalea bushes, cave vines, spore blossoms, or dripleaf. Do not break, place, or otherwise alter any blocks. If no suitable chamber is immediately visible, search vertically and horizontally around the staging point rather than returning to spawn.
steps.exact_input: Use movement controls and Space/Left Shift for vertical Spectator flight.
steps.success_cue: A well-lit or otherwise clearly visible underground chamber containing multiple generated Lush Caves decorative features is in view.

steps.action: Choose a stationary reference viewpoint from which several of the chamber's generated decorative blocks are visible at once. Avoid positioning the camera inside a block. Once the view is selected, stop moving.
steps.success_cue: The camera is stationary in open cave space and shows multiple identifiable generated decorative features.

steps.action: Press F3 to open the debug overlay. Record the displayed player X, Y, and Z coordinates as X_REF, Y_REF, and Z_REF. Also record the two camera rotation values shown on the Facing line as YAW_REF and PITCH_REF. Preserve negative signs and decimal values. These five values must be substituted into the second-world teleport command later.
steps.success_cue: X_REF, Y_REF, Z_REF, YAW_REF, and PITCH_REF have been saved outside the world and the player has not moved from the selected viewpoint.

steps.action: Capture a baseline screenshot while still at the recorded viewpoint. Keep the debug overlay visible so the image also preserves the location and facing information. Do not move before taking the screenshot.
steps.success_cue: Minecraft confirms that a screenshot was saved, and the player remains at the recorded reference viewpoint.

steps.action: Pause the game and return to the title screen without deleting or copying the first world.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Save and Quit to Title
steps.success_cue: The title screen is visible and the MC-238073-Baseline save remains available in the single-player world list.

steps.action: Open the single-player world list and begin creating a second, independent world. Do not duplicate or reopen the baseline save.
steps.success_cue: A fresh Create New World screen is open.

steps.action: Give the independently generated second world a distinct comparison name.
steps.success_cue: The world-name field contains MC-238073-Replica.

steps.action: Set the second world to the same Creative game mode and commands setting used for the baseline world.
steps.exact_input: Game Mode: Creative; Allow Cheats: ON
steps.success_cue: The second world's creation screen shows Creative mode and commands/cheats enabled.

steps.action: Open the additional world-generation options and enter exactly the same report seed used for the baseline world.
steps.exact_input: More World Options... -> Seed for the World Generator: -8718622960759467126
steps.success_cue: The second world's seed field contains exactly -8718622960759467126.

steps.action: Configure the second world with exactly the same custom world type and biome as the first world.
steps.exact_input: World Type: Single Biome -> Customize -> select Lush Caves -> Done
steps.success_cue: The second world is configured as a Single Biome Lush Caves world.

steps.action: Confirm that the second world's seed, world type, biome, and other world-generation options match the baseline settings, then create the world.
steps.success_cue: The game begins generating the independent MC-238073-Replica world.

steps.action: Wait for the second world to finish its initial loading and for movement and chat to respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The player can move normally and nearby spawn chunks are rendered in MC-238073-Replica.

steps.action: Verify that the second world received the required seed. Press T, enter the command with its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports exactly -8718622960759467126.

steps.action: Enter Spectator mode in the second world. Press T, enter the command with its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The player can fly and pass through blocks in MC-238073-Replica.

steps.action: Teleport to the exact baseline viewpoint and orientation. Replace X_REF, Y_REF, Z_REF, YAW_REF, and PITCH_REF with the five numeric values recorded in step 15; do not type the placeholder names or braces. Open chat with T, execute the completed command with its leading slash, and press Enter. This action loads or generates the second world's chunks at the reference location.
steps.success_cue: The debug coordinates and camera rotation in the second world match the recorded baseline values.

steps.action: Do not move or interact after teleporting. Wait until the reference chamber and all surrounding chunks have fully rendered and camera movement would respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The second world is fully rendered at the same recorded position and orientation used for the baseline screenshot, with the player stationary in Spectator mode.

stor.handoff_condition: The independently generated MC-238073-Replica world has just loaded the target chunks for seed -8718622960759467126, and the stationary Spectator camera is at the exact position and orientation recorded in the baseline world. Hand control to the observation subsystem with the step-16 baseline screenshot available for comparison.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a world type or target biome. Snapshot 21w10a is nevertheless the required recommended version because it is the first listed affected version. External version documentation confirms that Lush Caves in 21w10a are available through custom Single Biome world generation rather than the default world type, so this plan uses a Single Biome Lush Caves world.

The report supplies no comparison coordinates or individual decorator to inspect. The X=512, Y=32, Z=512 staging location and the procedure for dynamically recording a nearby decorator-rich chamber are practical choices intended to provide an exact location that can be revisited in the second world.
Creative mode, enabled commands, Spectator mode, the teleport commands, and the baseline screenshot are execution aids. The report does not state that these are required conditions of the bug.

The report says the same-seed creation may be repeated as many times as desired. This plan creates two independent worlds because two are the minimum needed to establish a baseline and a same-seed comparison state.
The unavailable report attachments may depict specific examples or locations, but the supplied report text does not identify any attachment as mandatory for reproduction.
